## Critique
- claim-1: Correctly grounded by [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 213-218].
- claim-2: Correctly grounded by [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 702-735].
- claim-3: Not established. The proposed \(F_{\rho,\sigma}\) is explicit and homogeneous, and the stated endpoint and boundary conventions are consistent. However, the “rectangle-attachment determinant lemma” is precisely the missing substantive assertion and is not proved. Map (3) is only an assignment on formal Hopf-index pairs; the Hopf identity does not imply that its image vanishes. No Jacobi–Trudi matrix, Laplace minors, signs, or bijection between nonboundary minors and \(\sigma\subsetneq\rho\) is displayed. Nor is a map from the accepted full-coordinate \(\operatorname{Lin}_\varphi\)-row identity to (2) defined. The graded-kernel presentation cannot supply this missing identity. Thus the quotient equation remains unresolved.

## Repair certificates
- [proof-attempt] Prove explicitly
  \[
  \sum_{\sigma\subseteq\rho}(-1)^{|\rho|-|\sigma|}
  \omega(s_{\rho/\sigma})s_{(i^j,\sigma)}
  =(-1)^{|\rho|}s_{(i+\rho'_1,\ldots,i+\rho'_b,i^{j-b})}.
  \]
  Give the actual determinant matrices, the complete minor indexing, and every Laplace sign. Equivalently, define a linear rectangle-attachment map on the full-coordinate row module and prove that it sends each Hopf term to the asserted Schur product and sends the complete accepted row relation to zero.
- [computation] Alternatively, disprove the equation by giving one admissible tuple and one \(\rho\subseteq b^a\), together with exact Schur-basis expansions whose difference has a specified nonzero coefficient. Finite agreement cannot prove the universal identity.
- [source-refresh] If the determinant identity is intended to be sourced, provide a bounded passage stating that exact rectangular identity with its hypotheses and signs; [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 702-735] supplies only the antipode identity.

## Required revisions
- Replace the unproved determinant-lemma assertion with the explicit proof above or a valid parameter counterexample.
- Explain why the attachment operation preserves the relevant full-coordinate relation; a termwise reassignment alone is insufficient.
- Retain the stated \(\rho=\varnothing\), \(a=0\), and \(b=j\) conventions, and conclude only the scoped certificate.
